news.title: PH 4-gold haul in Asiad matches 2018, 2022 wins
news.text: THE Philippines posted another 4-gold haul at the 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, matching its record in 2018 and 2022, but took home more silvers and bronzes — nine and 16, respectively — for a total of 29 medals.The slew of silvers and bronzes enabled the Philippines to achieve its best Asiad finish in terms of medal composition since its 7-gold, 6-silver, and 24-bronze haul at the 1962 edition in Jakarta, where the Philippines placed fifth overall.At press time on Saturday afternoon during the penultimate day of competitions, the Philippines stood in 16th place with a 4-9-16 gold-silver-bronze haul in a field of 45 countries.Philippine Sports Commission (PSC) Chairman Patrick Gregorio expressed satisfaction with the country’s performance.“We’re very happy that we won so many medals in so many sports — if I’m not mistaken, in 18 or 19 sports. In China [at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games], we won medals in 11 sports,” said Gregorio.“That is a major change, and that is what is important for the development of Philippine sports, particularly our grassroots program.”Redeeming himself from his so-so performance at the 2018 Asiad in Jakarta, gymnast Carlos Yulo seized two gold medals this time, winning titles in floor exercise and vault to lead the Filipino athletes.Yulo has now won in every major international competition — Asian Games, Asian Championships, Southeast Asian Games, World Championships, and the Olympics.Ernest John “EJ” Obiena delivered the Philippines’ second gold after defending his men’s pole vault title.Obiena secured his second straight gold medal in a record fashion, posting a 5.91m clearance to break his 5.90m in the previous edition in Hangzhou, China, back in 2023.A few gold medals and podium finishes slipped, especially after the controversial loss of boxer Carlo Paalam in the men’s 55kg final, the early exits of jiujitsu world champs Kimberly Custodio and Annie Ramirez, and the heartbreaking fourth-place finishes of swimmer Kayla Sanchez.Alex Eala lost to Wang Xiyu of China in the women’s singles semifinals at the 2026 Asian Games, replacing a gold hope for a bronze medal.Taekwondo jin Jeus Gabriel Derick Yape rose to somehow negate that with a surprise gold.Yape topped the mixed virtual taekwondo that enabled the Philippines to match its 4-gold haul from the previous Asiad edition in addition to his individual poomsae bronze.Tasked as the flag bearer in the closing ceremony on Sunday, Yape highlighted a best-ever 1-3-1 gold-silver-bronze haul by the Filipino jins at the Asiad.
news.author: Niel Victor C. Masoy

news.title: 5th gold eludes Philippines in Nagoya Asian Games
news.text: THE Philippines collected four golds, eight silvers and 16 bronzes as of 7 p.m. on Friday in the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.Philippine Olympic Committee (POC) President Abraham Tolentino had initially set a target of eight gold medals but will have to settle with four, matching its tally in the 2022 Hangzhou Games.The Philippines, however, has more medals than in 2022, when its athletes bought home two silvers and 12 bronzes for a total of 18 medals.Tachiana Mangin and Olympian Kurt Bryan Barbosa reached the finals in taekwondo Friday night, but had to settle for silvers.Mangin bowed to world taekwondo champion Jingyue Ma of China in the women’s under-49-kilogram (kg), 2-0, and Barbosa lost to Tamirlan Tleules of Kazakhstan, 2-0, in men’s under-58 kg.On Friday morning, Jeus Yape snared an unexpected gold for the nation after defeating Ngoc Tuyet Sang Chau of Vietnam, 2-0, in the mixed individual virtual taekwondo event at the Toyohashi Gymnasium.The 22-year-old became the first athlete to strike gold in the taekwondo discipline.He joins the elite club of gold medal finishers of this year’s Asiad with double-gold medalist Carlos Yulo and Ernest John “EJ” Obiena.Yulo dominated the men’s vault and floor exercise events, replicating his feat in the Paris 2024 Olympics.Obiena claimed a new Asian Games record of 5.91 meters, in the process defending his pole vault crown.Sports officials had targeted an eight-gold-medal haul in Nagoya, coming from jiu-jitsu, boxing, mixed martial arts, gymnastics, athletics, tennis and Esports.In mixed martial arts, Jean Paul Saclag lost to Otabek Rajabov of Tajikistan, settling for silver.The esports delegation, who received a special shout-out from the POC president during the send-off ceremony, finished with a bronze in Honor of Kings and Pokémon Unite.In the tennis event, Alexandra “Alex” Eala lost some gas at the semifinal round, bowing to Chinese Xiyu Wang, 6-3, 3-6, 2-6, to settle for third place.Olympian boxer Carlo Paalam was expected to deliver the country’s fifth gold on Friday, but he lost by split decision to Japan’s Rui Yamaguchi.In jiu-jitsu, 2022 Asiad gold medalist Annie Ramirez made an early exit, beaten by Thailand’s Nuchanat Singchalad in the Women’s –52 kg round of 16.The jiu-jitsu team delivered a bronze medal as Jenna Kaila Napolis bested Mongolia’s Tsagaanbileg Altangerel.The Philippines still hopes to add to its medal haul on Saturday when Andrea Lois Lao, Alexandria Luz Ramirez and Vito Luis Luzuriaga vie for a podium finish in jiu-jitsu.Baby Jessica Canabal faces Thailand’s Natkamon Wassana​ in the round of 16 in taekwondo, hoping to advance in the next round and finish the day with a medal.The women’s softball team looks to bag a bronze when it takes on Taiwan.Pauline Del Rosario, Bianca Isabel Pagdanganan and Rianne Mikaela Malixi vie for a medal in golf.The women’s pair of Danna Abbad and Joshea Malazarte guns for a bronze finish in padel.
news.author: Nicole Anne D.g. Bugauisan

news.title: Jeus Gabriel Yape notches gold in Asian Games, fourth for PH
news.text: (UPDATE) MANILA, Philippines — Jeus Gabriel Yape delivered the fourth gold for the Philippines after defeating Ngoc Tuyet Sang Chau of Vietnam, 2-0, in the mixed individual virtual taekwondo event at the 2026 Asian Games on Friday morning at the Toyohashi Gymnasium in Aichi, Japan.The 22-year-old Yape became the fourth Filipino to snare a gold medal in this year’s Asiad edition after two golds from Carlos Yulo and one from Ernest John “EJ” Obiena.With two days left, the Philippines has already tied its previous finish of four golds in the 2022 Hangzhou, China edition.Yape went against a 21-year-old female Vietnamese since the mixed individual event has no separate gender or weight class divisions.The mixed individual virtual taekwondo event is a digital, non-contact sport where athletes compete in a virtual arena.The athletes wear a headset and sensors, where their movements and motions are tracked in real time.Their characters will be represented on the screen as avatars and will fight in a virtual space with no physical contact with an opponent.The game is played as a best-of-three-round system, with each round lasting one minute.The athletes should execute kicks, side attacks, downward strikes, and head attacks to target the opponent's avatar, with their movements copied on the screen.Yape finished with a bronze on Thursday in the men’s individual poomsae competition.
news.author: Nicole Anne D.g. Bugauisan

news.title: POC chief says surpassing gold medal target still possible
news.text: Philippine Olympic Committee (POC) president Abraham “Bambol” Tolentino is confident the country would surpass its target of four gold medals in the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan.Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Tolentino said the country still has a strong chance in multiple disciplines, including jiu-jitsu and judo.“There are still three days until Sunday morning. Last 3 days, still hoping for more golds,” he said. His bold prediction, however, took a hit Thursday afternoon when top seed Alex Eala lost in women's tennis semifinals and settled for the bronze. At the previous Asian Games in Hangzhou, China, the Philippines finished with four gold medals from pole vaulter EJ Obiena, jiu-jitsu fighters Annie Ramirez and Meggie Ochoa, and the Gilas Pilipinas men’s basketball team.At press time, the Philippines has three gold medals, one from Obiena and two from Carlos Yulo.Tokyo Olympic silver medalist and pugilist Carlo Paalam and the jiu-jitsu fighters, including Ramirez and Kaila Napolis are still in the hunt for a gold medal.“God willing. Fellow Filipinos, let's pray for our athletes at Team Philippines. They’re still on the qualification stage. That’s why we can still surpass the four, hopefully,” Tolentino said.The POC chief earlier said that their target was to win four gold medals — later increased to eight — for this edition of the Asian Games.The closing ceremony is set to be held on Sunday with Japan handing over the Olympic Council of Asia flag to Doha, Qatar, which will host the quadrennial event for the second time in 2030.
news.author: Aric John Sy Cua

news.title: Paalam gets shot at Asian Games gold
news.text: FILIPINO boxer Carlo Paalam advanced to the 20th Asian Games men’s 55-kilogram (kg) class gold medal round after earning a close semifinal split decision win against Kazakh Makhmud Sabyrkhan at the Nishio Gymnasium in Japan on Wednesday afternoon.Three judges favored Paalam, 29-27, 29-28, 29-27, while two deemed Sabyrkhan the winner, 29-27, 30-26, in the slugfest.Throwing solid punches including a right straight that shook Sabyrkhan in the second round, Paalam secured a silver medal and his highest finish in the continental meet.The Olympic silver medalist snared a bronze at the 2018 Asiad edition in Indonesia.Coached by Elmer Pamisa, Paalam said the bout turned out to be a battle of tactical counters.“He’ll come forward, and I’ll just stick to my game. We’ll just make sure we’re the first to counter,” said Paalam.Paalam overcame a point deduction from the referee in the physical third round which he lost, 26-30.Digging deep into his endurance, Paalam said he showcased the immense Filipino fighting spirit to sway the judges in the last two rounds which he won, 29-28, 29-27.“I’m showing the referee that we’re Filipinos, that this is our blood. Even if we have to fight to the death, we’ll give it everything in the last round,” shared Paalam.As the last man standing among the Filipino contingent, Paalam gets himself a shot at ending the Philippines’ 16-year gold medal drought in Asiad boxing.Rey Saludar was the last Filipino boxer to win a gold in the Asian Games after ruling the 2010 flyweight division (52 kg) in Guangzhou, China.Paalam faces home bet Rui Yamaguchi in the final, looking to add to the Philippines’ three-gold haul in the ongoing meet after gymnast Carlos Yulo’s two and pole vaulter Ernest John “EJ” Obiena’s one.Yamaguchi defeated Mongolian Bilguunsaikhan Kharkhuu via unanimous decision in their semifinal encounter.The gold medal match is set for Oct. 2 at 12:45 p.m. in Manila.Receiving a first-round bye, Paalam started his campaign with a majority decision win over Indian Jadumani Singh Mandengbam in the second round (round of 16).Paalam then took down Chinese Zhang Jiamao in the quarterfinal via split decision before earning another one against Sabyrkhan in the semis.
news.author: Niel Victor C. Masoy

news.title: Obiena grateful after Asiad defense
news.text: UNDER wet conditions due to a drizzly Tuesday evening, Ernest John “EJ” Obiena still claimed his second straight men’s pole vault title in the 20th Asian Games in Japan.The Filipino pole vault ace did it in a record-setting fashion at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium.Obiena secured the gold medal after Chinese Yao Jie and Li Chenyang struck out at 5.75 m which the Philippine bet cleared in just one try.The 30-year-old decided to post a new meet record and successfully did so with a 5.91-meter (m) clearance, surpassing the 5.90-m height he aced in the previous edition in Hangzhou, China, back in 2023.Obiena thus gave the Philippines its third overall gold in the ongoing meet following gymnast Carlos Yulo’s floor exercise and vault titles.“A gold and a GR (games record) here in Nagoya,” wrote Obiena in his social media pages on Wednesday morning.“As athletes, we live in these moments. Moments that make us overthink, stress us, adrenaline pumping pressure on our backs and sometimes ... just sometimes pure joy. I take these moments as a blessing. This is what keeps me going back for more.”Obiena expressed gratitude to his team as well as the Filipinos for supporting him.“To all of the 110 million Filipinos, maraming salamat po (thank you so much) for making these moments possible. Competing is one thing, but competing for something greater, for the Philippines, is a privilege that I do not take lightly. For the country.”Obiena surpassed the 5.90-m height thrice this season, which he ended with this Asiad gold.Bouncing back from a lackluster 2025, the 6-foot-2 pole vaulter from Tondo collected 10 golds this year as he continued his resurgence.“What I felt today, it’s been a while, and to be honest I missed it,” Obiena said to POC Media.“With that, I think it’s bit of a reborn that I see the sport in a much different perspective than it was, a little bit of fun and reality”
news.author: Niel Victor C. Masoy

news.title: Asian Games | Day 10: China sweeps sprint relays as An retains badminton crown
news.text:
by sportswriter Li Jia

NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 29 (Xinhua) -- Seventeen-year-old sprint sensation Chen Yujie led China to gold in the inaugural mixed 4x100m relay on Tuesday, while South Korea's An Se-young became the first player to retain the badminton women's singles title at the 2026 Asian Games.

A strong finish from Chen Yujie propelled China past Thailand to win the mixed 4x100m relay. The quartet of Chen Jinfeng, Liu Guoyi, Shi Junhao and Chen Yujie clocked a season-best 40.78 seconds.

The victory gave Chen Yujie her third gold medal in a spectacular Asian Games debut, following her titles in the women's 100m and 4x100m relay. She also won silver in the 200m.

China completed a sweep of all three 4x100m relay titles. Thailand took silver in 40.87, while India claimed bronze in 41.06.

Elsewhere on the final day of athletics, China's Zhang Jiale broke the Asian record to win the women's hammer throw with 78.27 meters. Zhang's compatriot Zhao Jie took silver, while Japan's Joy Iris McArthur got bronze.

China's Wu Hongjiao won the women's 800m, while Japan's Ko Ochiai took the men's title in a Games-record 1:44.48. In the men's pole vault, Ernest John Obiena of the Philippines cleared a Games-record 5.91 meters to win gold, ahead of China's Yao Jie and Li Chenyang.

As the badminton competition also concluded, South Korean world No. 1 An reinforced her dominance by claiming a second consecutive women's singles gold. The 24-year-old defeated home favorite and world No. 3 Akane Yamaguchi 21-17, 21-9 in the final.

"It really does feel like a dream. I am so happy," said An, who has lost just once in 57 matches this season. "Everything I put into it keeps coming back to me. It is overwhelming."

South Korea also won the women's doubles, with Lee So-hee and Baek Ha-na defeating China's Liu Shengshu and Tan Ning in three games.

In the men's doubles, newly crowned world champions Liang Weikeng and Wang Chang of China took the opening game 21-19, but Indonesia's Leo Rolly Carnando and Daniel Marthin fought back to win the next two 21-13, 21-18 and claim gold.

Thailand's Kunlavut Vitidsarn won the men's singles title by defeating Singapore's former world champion Loh Kean Yew 21-12, 21-16.

China took the mixed doubles title as Jiang Zhenbang and Wei Yaxin rallied from 18-13 down in the opening game to beat Indonesia's Amri Syahnawi and Nita Violina Marwah 21-19, 21-8.

China finished the badminton competition with two gold, three silver and three bronze medals.

Surfing made its Asian Games debut at Aichi-Nagoya, with the men's and women's shortboard competitions also serving as qualifiers for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

China's first Olympic surfer, 17-year-old Yang Siqi, took silver in the women's shortboard after losing to Japan's Mirai Ikeda in the final. In the men's event, Japan's Tokyo Olympic silver medalist Kanoa Igarashi defeated Indonesia's I Made Pajar Ariyana to win gold.

The weightlifting witnessed Iraq's Ali Ammar Yusur Rubaiawi lift 219kg in the snatch to set a world record in the men's over 110kg competition. He finished with a total of 465kg to take silver, while Iran's Ali Davoudi won gold with 466kg.

Uzbekistan's Akbar Djuraev also broke the snatch world record with 197kg on his way to the men's 110kg title. China won both the women's 86kg and over 86kg divisions.

In the pool, China continued its diving dominance with two more titles as Chen Yuxi won the women's 10m platform and Wang Zongyuan triumphed on the men's 3m springboard.

China also struck gold in both team sprint events as track cycling got underway. The women's team successfully defended its title in an Asian-record 45.370 seconds.

China added another gold in the women's trap team event in shooting.

In the women's football, China lost 2-0 to DPR Korea in the semifinals, while Japan beat South Korea by the same score in the other semifinal.

Bahrain edged defending champion Qatar 33-32 to win the men's handball title. ■

news.title: WATCH: PISTON continues strike; Manibela calls off protest
news.text: Good day. Welcome to The Manila Times where we bring you stories that shape our world. Today is September 30th.Our top story.Transport group Piston continued its nationwide strike for the second day. Piston said it is calling for lower fuel prices and the removal of taxes on petroleum products. Another transport group, Manibela, meanwhile, called off its protest. It also reiterated that it is a nonpartisan organization. Manibela said that it did not support or oppose political personalities based on their names or political affiliations. It stressed that its position was based on issues affecting public transport workers.Read more: https://tmt.ph/2435179Two-time Asian Games pole vault champion EJ Obiena says competing for the Philippines is a privilege he does not take lightly. Obiena made the remark after winning the gold medal in the men's pole vault event in record-setting fashion. He expressed gratitude to his team and the millions of Filipinos supporting him. The 30-year-old posted a new Asian Games record with a 5.91-meter clearance. This surpassed the previous Asiad record he set in China in 2023. Obiena described such moments in competitions as pure joy and a blessing. He said this is what keeps him going back for more.Read more: https://tmt.ph/2435662Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon inspected the status of the ongoing repair and rehabilitation of the Philippine General Hospital in Manila. Several unfinished infrastructure projects exist within the hospital complex, including one aimed at flood mitigation. The flood control project is intended to help protect patients, healthcare workers, and hospital facilities from flooding during heavy rainfall. The other projects are designed to enhance patient safety, support hospital operations, and ensure the continuous delivery of healthcare services.Senator Erwin Tulfo has filed a bill seeking to institutionalize a single Philippine tourism campaign slogan. The bill directs the Department of Tourism to formulate the official slogan and maintain it for a minimum of 15 years. He said frequent slogan changes weaken brand recognition and risk confusing international travelers. Tulfo noted that the Philippines is the only country that keeps changing things with every administration. He contrasted the Philippines’ approach with Malaysia’s long-running brand of “Malaysia, Truly Asia.”For more news and information, read The Manila Times in print, subscribe to its digital edition or log on to www.manilatimes.net.Follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X, TikTok and LinkedIn; and be part of our communities on Viber, Telegram, WhatsApp and Mastodon. That's all for now on The Manila Times Newscast.Stay tuned for more updates throughout the day, and remember to stay safe, stay informed, and stay connected.
